rows.summary: This research revises thermodynamic dissipation bounds by integrating information-theoretic constraints with memory dynamics in nonequilibrium systems. It establishes that predictive control in information engines is fundamentally limited by the interplay between memory retention energy costs, information-processing speed, and the precision of the underlying physical causal records. Specifically, generalized Thermodynamic Uncertainty Relations (TURs) provide tighter bounds for systems operating under finite-memory or non-equilibrium steady-state conditions compared to original, unconstrained formulations.
